resources.string: Risks, responsibility and terms of use
DSU Next is a tool for developers and advanced users. It changes how your device boots and how its storage is allocated. By continuing you accept every risk described on this page.

DSU Next is made for developers and advanced users who understand dynamic system updates, GSI images and Android storage. If you are not comfortable recovering a device on your own, do not use this tool.

Installing a dynamic system can lead to data loss, failed or looping boots, unexpected reboots, degraded performance, exhausted storage and, in the worst case, a device that no longer starts. Some of these problems only show up after the installation has finished. Images from unofficial or untrusted sources can be incompatible with your device or behave in ways nobody can predict.

You MUST have an unlocked bootloader. Installing images with a locked bootloader may be dangerous on some devices.
You MUST have a way to restore your device to its stock firmware.
A full backup of your data is RECOMMENDED.
Make sure the image matches your device and Android version.

You alone are responsible for what you do with this tool: the images you choose, the options you enable and the permissions you grant. Any damage caused by negligence, carelessness or ignoring the warnings shown in the app is entirely your responsibility.

DSU Next is provided \"as is\" and \"as available\", without warranty of any kind, express or implied. That includes any warranty of fitness for a particular purpose, reliability, or that it will work on your device. Features may change or stop working at any time.

To the maximum extent permitted by law, the developer is not liable for any damage, data loss, device malfunction, loss of warranty or any other harm that results from your negligence or from using this tool, even if the developer was told such harm was possible.

DSU Next is based in part on DSU Sideloader and uses open source libraries under their own licenses. The developer does not provide, verify or endorse any system image you install and is not responsible for it.
Tapping \"I agree\" confirms that you have read, understood and accepted this page. If you do not agree, close the app and do not use it.

Your kernel is likely to be registering f2fs in a different path than the one expected by the GSI daemon, there are some fixes you can try:\n - Use a module that ships a gsid binary which handles f2fs_dev.\n - Changing kernel.

Looks like SELinux denials are preventing DSU installation, there are some fixes you can try:
 - Use a module that ships sepolicy fixes for gsid.
 - If you're using a sdcard, try to unmount it (there is an option for that in settings section).
 - Change your SELinux to permissive (not recommended, weakens your device security).
On Android 10 devices, images/filesystem needs to have more than 512 extents, there are some fixes you can try:\n - Use a module that ships a patched gsid binary.
